column3: NKJV lacks “they kept coming up to Him,” as does the Textus Receptus; the critical text includes it.
NKJV has “our law,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the law.”
NKJV has “to crucify You, and power to release You,” reversing the Greek order (“release … crucify”), as in the Textus Receptus.
NKJV has “and led Him away,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text ends with “they took Jesus.”
NKJV has “Hebrew, Greek, and Latin,” following the Textus Receptus order; the critical text has “Hebrew, Latin, Greek.”
NKJV has “they filled a sponge with sour wine,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “putting a sponge full of the sour wine.”
